sites.rationale: ADORA1 is a GPCR with no signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–9 extracellular and TM1 beginning at residue 10, leaving 9 residues between the prepend junction and the first TM helix (well above the ≥3-residue minimum). No residue number is stated in any ledger line, but the N-terminus is the sole extracellular terminus of this receptor, so topology_derived applies and insert_after_residue=0 is the unique solution. Three independent papers (PMC6974774, PMC4513639, PMC12229354) with three different tags (HiBiT, FLAG/SF-TAP, Myc) all report tolerated N-terminal extracellular tags on the full-length membrane-anchored receptor, converging on this single junction. HiBiT–A1AR full-length construct expressed in HEK293 cells; NanoBiT complementation with exogenous purified LgBiT confirms cell-surface display of the N-terminally tagged receptor; agonist-induced internalization was subsequently monitored with this construct, demonstrating functional receptor trafficking. L7 (PMC4513639) independently reports N-terminal FLAG and SF-TAP tags on the same receptor. L9/L10 (PMC12229354) report a Myc tag engineered onto the 'extracellular region' of hA1R confirmed by flow cytometry; ADORA1 has no signal peptide and its only extracellular terminus is the N-terminus (residues 1–9), making this topology-derived to the same junction. sources.claim: NanoBiT has provided a platform for assessing protein–protein interactions in vitro in real time. 24 , 30 – 32 Here, we have used the NanoBiT complementation technology to monitor the presence of the human A 1 receptor, tagged on its N-terminus with HiBiT, at the cell surface of living cells following addition of purified LgBiT ( Fig. 1a ).

literature_notes: L5 disqualified: the FLAG-tagged A1R plasmid is from a commercial vendor (Sinobiological) and the tag position within the construct is unstated. L6 disqualified: eYFP is fused to the C-terminus, which is intracellular (residues 291–326). L8 disqualified: the YFP tag position on the A1R-Y288A mutant construct is not stated in the clip; Y288 is a point mutation within TM7 (residues 268–290), not a tag insertion site, and the YFP is most likely at the intracellular C-terminus. All three qualifying independent papers (L1–L4, L7, L9–L10) converge on the same N-terminal prepend junction, so only one site is reported.
